name: Lead Pipeline: WhatsApp Replies + Calendar Booking

parameters.content:
## Lead Pipeline: WhatsApp Replies + Calendar Booking
The lead replies on WhatsApp (button tap or free text). An LLM extracts the intent and the proposed time as JSON. Code validates the slot (future, business hours), Google Calendar checks free/busy, the event is created, and then read back to prove the booking really exists before anyone is told it worked.
Every critical failure lands in one handler: the lead gets a booking link, ops gets a Slack alert, the failure is logged.

### Signature verification
The webhook runs with Raw Body on, because Meta signs the exact raw bytes. The Code node recomputes the HMAC-SHA256 (sha256=...) header with the app secret from META_APP_SECRET and compares it in constant time. In n8n, env access inside Code nodes needs N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=false; a placeholder constant keeps the file importable offline.

### Why a direct LLM HTTP call, not an agent node
Slot extraction is one strict JSON extraction, so this uses a plain OpenAI chat completions call with JSON mode and a Postgres backed conversation history (pipeline_events). It keeps the workflow importable in a stock n8n with a single API key env var. The @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent node in this install can replace the two extraction nodes later without touching the rest of the flow. The model is told to never invent a time: an unclear reply returns a null slot and the lead is asked to pick from the booking link.

### Booking race safety
Free/busy is a check, not a lock. Two leads can pass it together, so after creating the event the workflow reads it back and compares summary and start time. A mismatch deletes the event, alerts ops, and offers alternatives instead of double booking quietly.
